references.text: Moses gave the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan, to the tribe of Gad, the tribe of Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
The descendants of Reuben and Gad asked to settle east of the Jordan because the land was suitable for livestock.
Moses describes the distribution of the land east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
The Lord gave the land to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh as their inheritance.
Joshua reminds Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh that they received their inheritance east of the Jordan from Moses.
Confirms that Reuben and Gad received their inheritance on the east side of the Jordan, which Moses gave them.
Moses had given the two and a half tribes an inheritance on the other side of the Jordan.
Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh had already received their inheritance east of the Jordan.
The two and a half tribes are sent back to their inherited land east of the Jordan.
